      "kind": "theorem",

items.informal_name: Order of Negative Multivariate Power Series: $\operatorname{order}(-f) = \operatorname{order}(f)$
items.type: ∀ {σ : Type u_1} {R : Type u_3} [inst : Ring R] (f : MvPowerSeries σ R), (-f).order = f.order
items.informal_description: For any multivariate power series $ f $, the order of $-f$ is equal to the order of $ f $, i.e., $\operatorname{order}(-f) = \operatorname{order}(f)$.

items.informal_name: Invariance of Sign Variations Under Polynomial Negation
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Ring R] [inst_1 : LinearOrder R] [IsOrderedRing R] (P : Polynomial R),
  (-P).signVariations = P.signVariations
items.informal_description: For any polynomial $ P $, the number of sign variations in $ -P $ is equal to the number of sign variations in $ P $, i.e., $ \operatorname{signVariations}(-P) = \operatorname{signVariations}(P) $.

items.informal_name: Order of Vanishing is Invariant Under Negation
items.type:
∀ {𝕜 : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} [inst : NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [inst_1 : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [inst_2 : NormedSpace 𝕜 E] {f : 𝕜 → E} {z₀ : 𝕜}, analyticOrderAt (-f) z₀ = analyticOrderAt f z₀
items.informal_description: The order of vanishing of the function $-f$ at $z_0$ is equal to the order of vanishing of $f$ at $z_0$, i.e., $\operatorname{ord}_{z_0}(-f) = \operatorname{ord}_{z_0}(f)$.

items.type: ∀ {R : Type u_2} [inst : Ring R] (φ : PowerSeries R), (-φ).order = φ.order
items.informal_description: For any univariate power series $\varphi$ over a ring $R$, the order of $-\varphi$ is equal to the order of $\varphi$, i.e., $\operatorname{ord}(-\varphi) = \operatorname{ord}(\varphi)$.

items.informal_name: Weighted Order is Invariant Under Negation of Multivariate Power Series
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} (w : σ → ℕ) {R : Type u_3} [inst : Ring R] (f : MvPowerSeries σ R),
  MvPowerSeries.weightedOrder w (-f) = MvPowerSeries.weightedOrder w f
items.informal_description: For any multivariate power series $ f $ over a ring $ R $ in variables indexed by $ \sigma $, and for any weight function $ w : \sigma \to \mathbb{N} $, the weighted order of $ -f $ with respect to $ w $ is equal to the weighted order of $ f $, i.e., $ (-f).\text{weightedOrder}\, w = f.\text{weightedOrder}\, w $. The weighted order measures the minimal weighted degree of non-zero terms in the series, and this equality shows that negation does not affect this invariant.

items.informal_name: Multiplicity of $ a $ in $ -b $ Equals Multiplicity in $ b $
items.type: ∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : Ring α] (a b : α), multiplicity a (-b) = multiplicity a b
items.informal_description: For any elements $ a $ and $ b $ in a ring, the multiplicity of $ a $ in $ -b $ is equal to the multiplicity of $ a $ in $ b $. This equality holds because negation does not affect the highest power of $ a $ dividing $ b $.
